az_alcove.blurb: A small bouldering pocket on the Catalina Highway side of Mount Lemmon, set toward the back of a canyon beyond the Hairpin Boulders. A cliff wall with boulders around the other sides gives it an enclosed, mellow feel. Five problems run from V0 up to V4, so most of it suits newer boulderers, with a single harder line. The best-known problem is a V0-1 traverse about 30 feet tall that finishes by downclimbing from a ledge, which makes it more of an adventure than a typical low boulder. Sun exposure here has not been described.

az_main_wall_5.blurb: A trad wall in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, tucked directly behind the Fist Pinnacle. It rises to roughly 125 feet at its tallest and offers long single-pitch lines. Five trad routes are known here, from an easy 5.7 up to 5.10 climbs, with four of the five at the harder end. Features include a crack that splits the wall, a line that goes over an arch and one that begins in a chimney and exits through a hole onto a boulder. Bring a normal trad rack. The walk from the parking areas takes about half an hour and follows a lightly cairned path through boulders and slabs.

az_creature_boulder.blurb: A single feature boulder in the East Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, reached by walking uphill from the meadow and following cairns to a tight squeeze between two large boulders. Beyond a small hole sits a little cave room where the main lines start. It is described as one of the better roof boulders in the area, with two lines leaving the cave and another hidden one reached through a gap. Five problems range from a V2 up to a V7, with a couple of V4s and a V5 in the middle. Expect overhanging, roof-style movement rather than easy slabs.

az_warhead.blurb: A large boulder with an amphitheater on its back side, in the Cochise Trail Boulders group of the East Stronghold at Cochise Stronghold. It sits just uphill from a neighbouring boulder called Flat Top; a tunnel behind Flat Top leads toward it. Five problems cover a wide spread, from an easy V2 through a pair around V5 up to a V8 and a hard V10. Two of the lines are marked as classics. The wider boulder cluster is a short walk from the campground along the Cochise Trail, with the boulders off the right side of the path between the trail and a stream bed.

az_ski_jump.blurb: A huge boulder in the Cochise Trail Boulders group of the East Stronghold, visible from the trail and shaped a bit like an iceberg. Its overhanging face is covered in chickenhead holds. Five problems range from a V2 through a V4 and two V6s up to a V8, and a couple carry a risk rating, so the harder lines call for care with pads and spotters. To reach it, drop from the slabs by the trail down to the stream, pass another boulder, climb over a big flat rock on the left side of the creek and head uphill. Sun exposure here has not been described.
